title: Condensed coefficient localization is exact and commutes with cohomology
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $u:V\to S$ be an object of its small pro-étale site [sk-def-pe-site]. Let $\Gamma$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and put $\Gamma_T=p_T^*\Gamma$ for schemes $T$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use sectionwise module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and the ringed-topos module pullback
$$u^*F=\Gamma_V\otimes_{u^{-1}\Gamma_S}u^{-1}F$$
with the canonical coefficient isomorphism $\alpha_u:u^{-1}\Gamma_S\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma_V$ [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms, sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. Then:

(1) The forgetful functor identifies $V_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with the localized site $S_{\mathrm{proét}}/V$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], including its covering families. Under this identification $u^{-1}$ on abelian sheaves is sectionwise restriction. The map $\alpha_u$ identifies $\Gamma_S|_V$ with $\Gamma_V$ as ring sheaves, compatibly with all section restriction maps and multiplication by sections. Transport of module actions along this ring isomorphism is an equivalence, and there is a natural isomorphism from $u^*$ to sectionwise localized module restriction followed by this transport. In particular, at every $W\to V$, the underlying abelian group of $u^*F$ is canonically $F(W\to S)$, with the action transported by $\alpha_u(W)$. The functor $u^*$ is additive and exact, meaning that it preserves finite limits and finite colimits.

(2) In the unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], let $D(u^*)$ be the functor induced by termwise $u^*$. If a cochain complex $K^\bullet$ represents $Q\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(\Gamma_S))$, then the termwise sectionwise restriction of $K^\bullet$, with its coefficient actions transported as in (1), represents $D(u^*)Q$. For every $q\in\mathbf Z$ there is a natural isomorphism
$$u^*H^q(Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(D(u^*)Q),$$
induced on a representative by the restriction identifications of kernels and images and the quotient onto cohomology. No boundedness, flatness, finite-presentation, quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness or admissibility hypothesis is imposed.
